summary: Only the statement layer of stage RD.2 was read in this session: Kedlaya's formulation of the p-adic local monodromy theorem (quasi-unipotence of (σ,∇)-modules over the Robba ring), the slope filtration theorem for σ-modules (Theorem 1.2 / 6.10) and the reduction of the former to the latter via Tsuzuki's unit-root theorem, as described in Sections 1.1-1.4 of arXiv:math/0110124v4. The drafter read no proof from Chapters 2-6 and examined no other stage; all other stages are recorded as not read. The packet records the exact hypotheses (choice of Frobenius σ, finite extension of Γ_con, residual separability when k is perfect) so that RD.2's consumers (RD.5, PadicHodgeTheory R06.3) do not import a weaker statement. Independent review (REVIEW-EXT-03, 2026-09-15) re-fetched the same arXiv version (identical SHA-256) and additionally read the definitions of Section 2.5, Theorem 6.10 with proof and Sections 6.4-6.5 (Proposition 6.11, Theorems 6.12-6.13 with proofs), and the passage of Berger, Representations p-adiques et equations differentielles, where the monodromy theorem is consumed. The node statements now carry the source hypotheses and the precise and logarithmic forms; Chapters 2-5 and Proposition 6.9 remain unread.

nodes.title: Quasi-unipotent (σ,∇)-modules and the p-adic local monodromy theorem (Theorem 1.1, precise form 6.12, logarithmic form 6.13)
nodes.statement: Definitions (Section 1.1, repeated in Section 2.5): for a ring R with p ≠ 0 and a ring endomorphism σ, a σ-module is a finite locally free R-module M with an R-linear map F: M ⊗_{R,σ} R → M that becomes an isomorphism over R[1/p]; a (σ,∇)-module is a σ-module with a connection ∇: M → M ⊗ Ω^1_{R/O} (Leibniz rule) such that ∇∘F = (F⊗dσ)∘∇. A (σ,∇)-module M over the Robba ring Γ_an,con is quasi-unipotent if, after tensoring Γ_an,con over Γ_con with a finite extension of Γ_con, M admits a filtration by (σ,∇)-submodules whose successive quotients admit a basis of elements in the kernel of ∇ (if k is perfect one may also insist that the extension of Γ_con be residually separable). Theorem 1.1 (local monodromy theorem): for any Frobenius σ for Γ_an,con, every (σ,∇)-module over Γ_an,con is quasi-unipotent. Precise form, Theorem 6.12: for a (σ,∇)-module M over Γ_an,con = Γ^{k((t))}_an,con, the filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ ... ⊂ M_l = M of Theorem 6.10 (slope-filtration node) satisfies (d) each M_i is a (σ,∇)-submodule; (e) each N_i is ∇-stable; (f) there is a finite nearly separable extension K/k((t)) (separable if k is perfect) such that each N_i is spanned by the kernel of ∇ over Γ^K_con[1/p]; (g) if k is algebraically closed, N_i is isomorphic over Γ^K_con[1/p] to a direct sum of standard (σ,∇)-modules. The source states that Theorem 1.1 follows immediately. Logarithmic form, Theorem 6.13: for some finite (nearly) separable extension K of k((t)), M admits a basis over Γ^K_log,an,con (isomorphic to Γ^K_an,con[log z] for any z ∈ Γ^K_con lifting a uniformizer of K) consisting of elements of the kernel of ∇; if k is algebraically closed, M decomposes over Γ^K_log,an,con as a direct sum of standard (σ,∇)-submodules. Remark (Section 1.1, marked 'not needed in this paper'): for a given ∇, whether a compatible F exists does not depend on σ, by Tsuzuki's change-of-Frobenius functors [T2, Theorem 3.4.10].
hypotheses: k is a field of characteristic p > 0 (not assumed perfect) and O is a finite totally ramified extension of a Cohen ring C(k). Γ_an,con is the ring of Laurent series over O[1/p] converging on some open annulus with outer radius 1; Γ_con ⊂ Γ_an,con is the subring of series taking integral values on some such annulus, a discrete valuation ring (Section 1.1; the precise definitions of Chapter 2 were read only in Section 2.5).

σ is a Frobenius for Γ_an,con in Kedlaya's sense: a composition power of a ring endomorphism preserving Γ_con and reducing modulo a uniformizer of Γ_con to the p-th power map (for example t^σ = t^q for t ∈ Γ_con lifting a uniformizer of k((t))). No Frobenius exists on the functions on a fixed annulus, which is why the Robba ring is used.
Modules are finite locally free; over the Bézout rings used they are free (Proposition 2.5, cited at lines 118 and 791, statement not read).

The Frobenius structure is a hypothesis of Theorem 1.1. The inspected passages contain no counterexample for connections without Frobenius: Section 1.2 only records that the Christol-Mebkhout weight filtration exists with or without Frobenius and that André and Mebkhout prove quasi-unipotence of its graded pieces when a Frobenius structure is present. The stage acceptance test (removing Frobenius must not leave the theorem available) still needs a sourced example.

Quasi-unipotence allows a finite extension of Γ_con (a finite cover of the annulus), not only an extension of the coefficient field. Theorem 6.12 realizes it with a finite nearly separable K/k((t)) (separable if k is perfect); the auxiliary finite extension O'/O used in the proof of (f) is removed there.

Drafter scope: Sections 1.1-1.4. Reviewer scope: Theorem 6.10 with proof and Sections 6.4-6.5 with proofs. Their inputs from Chapters 3-5 and Proposition 6.9, and Tsuzuki [T1], were not read (see gaps).
proofSteps: Strategy (Sections 1.2 and 1.4): isolate the Frobenius structure and prove the slope filtration theorem for σ-modules over Γ_an,con (Theorem 1.2/6.10) by trivializing σ-modules over auxiliary big rings and descending. Then use the connection only on the pure-slope pieces N_i, where Tsuzuki's unit-root theorem applies (Proposition 6.11).

Theorem 6.12(d), pp. 81-82: by induction on rank it suffices to treat i = 1; after enlarging O and twisting, the special slopes lie in the value group of O and s_1 = 0. Choose a basis of N_1 on which F acts by an invertible matrix X over Γ_con (Proposition 5.8) and extend it to M, so F = [[X, Y], [0, Z]] and ∇ = [[P, Q], [R, S]]. The relation ∇∘F = (F⊗dσ)∘∇ gives RX = (du^σ/du)ZR^σ. With X = U^{-1}U^σ (Proposition 5.11), Z = V^{-1}DV^σ (D scalar with entries of positive valuation), du^σ/du = μx with |μ| < 1, and y^σ = xy (Proposition 3.18), this becomes yVRU^{-1} = μD(yVRU^{-1})^σ, and Proposition 3.19(c) forces R = 0.

Theorem 6.12(e): the top-left corner gives yUPU^{-1} + yUX_1U^{-σ} = μ(yUPU^{-1})^σ with X_1 = dX/du. Proposition 3.19(c) puts the entries of P in Γ^alg_con ∩ Γ_an,con = Γ_con, so N_1 is ∇-stable. The source attributes this to Berger [Bg, Lemme V.14] but gives its own proof.

Theorem 6.12(f): under the simplifying assumptions N_1 is a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over Γ_con, so Proposition 6.11 gives a finite (nearly) separable K with kernel of ∇ of full rank. In general the kernel has full rank only after a finite extension O'/O, and decomposing kernel elements along an O-basis of O' descends them; the printed "which span M" must mean that they span N_1. For (g), with k algebraically closed, the kernel of ∇ is F-stable and Dieudonné-Manin (Theorem 5.6) splits it into standard modules.

Proposition 6.11, pp. 79-80: for k algebraically closed and q = p this is Tsuzuki [T1, Theorem 5.1.1]. The case q = p^f applies that result to the (σ_0,∇_0)-module M_0 ⊕ ... ⊕ M_{f-1} built from Frobenius pullbacks and projects to the first factor. For general k, a compactness argument over the inverse system T_S of partial solutions descends kernel elements from the completed maximal unramified extension O' of O to O. The (nearly) separable choice of K uses Proposition 5.10 and Dieudonné-Manin in the form of Proposition 5.5. The proof does not argue for the existence of a finite K on which F satisfies v_p(A - I) > 1/(p-1); that input sits inside the Tsuzuki citation.

Theorem 1.1 from Theorem 6.12: each M_i/M_{i-1} is spanned over Γ_an,con by N_i, which is spanned by horizontal elements over Γ^K_con[1/p]. This is the filtration that quasi-unipotence requires ("Theorem 1.1 follows immediately", p. 80).

Theorem 6.13, p. 83: by Theorem 6.12 choose a basis v_1, ..., v_n of M over Γ^K_an,con with ∇v_i ∈ SatSpan(v_1, ..., v_{i-1}) ⊗ Ω^1, and inductively set w_i = v_i − Σ_{j<i} e_{i,j} w_j with de_{i,j}/du = c_{i,j}, using that every expression u^l (log u)^m is a derivative of a linear combination of such expressions. The source justifies this only by "recall from calculus"; it does not discuss convergence of the termwise antiderivatives of the infinite sums c_{i,j}. Its indices are misprinted ("∇v_i = Σ_{j<i} A_ij v_i", "put ∇v_j = ...").

Alternative proofs: André and Mebkhout prove Theorem 1.1 through the Christol-Mebkhout weight filtration of the connection (Section 1.2). The atlas stage records these as alternative sources requiring separate conventions.
acceptance: Bessel isocrystal (Section 1.5, pp. 7-8; p odd, O = Z_p[π] with π^{p-1} = −p, t^σ = t^p): a rank-two (σ,∇)-module with generic Newton slopes 0 and 1 becomes unipotent only over Γ_an,con[y] with y = (t/4)^{1/2}, and both of its special slopes equal 1/2. This checks that the permitted extension is a finite extension of Γ_con (here obtained by adjoining a square root of t), not a coefficient extension.

Nilpotent form (abstract, p. 1: "the module admits a basis over a finite cover of the annulus on which the connection acts via a nilpotent matrix"): in the proof of Theorem 6.13 this is the basis v_1, ..., v_n with ∇v_i ∈ SatSpan(v_1, ..., v_{i-1}) ⊗ Ω^1. The stage test that a unipotent logarithmic extension has nilpotent residue is a consequence still to be derived; no residue computation is displayed in the source.

Downstream uses named in Section 1.3 (not acceptance tests): finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology with overconvergent F-isocrystal coefficients ([Cr2] for curves, [Ke7] = math.AG/0208027 in general; RD.5); p-adic Weil II ([Ke8] = math.NT/0210149; RD.6 through RD.5); Tsuzuki's full faithfulness conjecture ([Ke6]); Berger's deduction of the p-adic monodromy conjecture ([Bg]; R06.3, see the link annotation).

nodes.title: Slope filtration of σ-modules over the Robba ring and reduction of local monodromy to the unit-root case (statements)
nodes.statement: Theorem 1.2 (Section 1.2): every σ-module M over Γ_an,con has a canonical filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ ... ⊂ M_l = M by saturated σ-submodules such that (a) each M_i/M_{i-1} is isomorphic over Γ_an,con to a σ-module N_i defined over Γ_con[1/p]; (b) the slopes of N_i are all equal to a rational number s_i; (c) s_1 < ... < s_l. Precise form, Theorem 6.10: (a) M_i/M_{i-1} has a single special slope s_i; (b) s_1 < ... < s_l; (c) M_i/M_{i-1} contains an F-stable Γ_con[1/p]-submodule N_i of the same rank which spans M_i/M_{i-1} over Γ_an,con and has all generic slopes equal to s_i. Conditions (a) and (b) determine the filtration uniquely, and the N_i are unique; this uniqueness is what "canonical" means in the source. Slopes: the Dieudonné-Manin classification, stated in part in Section 1.2 and precisely in Section 5.2 (unread), says that over R[1/p], for R a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0,p) with algebraically closed residue field, every σ-module is isomorphic to a direct sum of standard modules M_{λ,d} (λ ∈ O[1/p], d ≥ 1; F v_1 = v_2, ..., F v_{d-1} = v_d, F v_d = λ v_1) of slope v_p(λ)/d, and the slopes that occur do not depend on the decomposition. For a discrete valuation ring R of mixed characteristic the slopes of a σ-module over R[1/p] are those of a Dieudonné-Manin decomposition over the maximal unramified extension of the completion of R (the generic slopes over Γ_con); Γ_an,con is not a discrete valuation ring, so its special slopes come from the filtration over the auxiliary ring Γ^alg_an,con of Chapter 4. Section 1.2 says that Theorem 1.2 together with Tsuzuki's unit-root theorem [T1] "makes it possible to deduce" Theorem 1.1. The deduction actually given (Section 6.4) also needs the ∇-stability statements of Theorem 6.12(d)-(e), recorded in the local-monodromy node.
hypotheses: Same base as the local-monodromy node: k of characteristic p > 0, O finite totally ramified over a Cohen ring C(k), Γ_con ⊂ Γ_an,con, and σ a Frobenius for Γ_an,con in Kedlaya's sense (a composition power of an endomorphism preserving Γ_con and lifting the p-th power map). σ-modules are finite locally free with F an isomorphism after inverting p.
Γ_an,con is not a discrete valuation ring, so slopes cannot be defined directly over it; the filtration theorem makes the reduction to Γ_con possible (Section 1.2).
Tsuzuki's theorem [T1, Theorem 5.1.1] on unit-root (σ,∇)-modules is imported (Proposition 6.11) and not read; Section 1.2 notes that it also specifies the extension needed.

Drafter scope: statements in Sections 1.1-1.4. Reviewer scope: Theorem 6.10 with proof (pp. 77-78). That proof relies on Proposition 6.9, Proposition 5.16, Corollary 3.16, Propositions 4.4-4.5 and Proposition 5.11, none of which were read.
proofSteps: Plan (Section 1.4): Chapter 2 recalls the Robba ring, its integral subring Γ_con and the completion Γ (the Amice ring). Chapter 3 builds auxiliary rings after de Jong, notably Γ^alg_an,con, and shows that it is Bézout. Chapter 4 equips every σ-module over the Robba ring with a canonical filtration over Γ^alg_an,con (special Newton polygon), and Chapter 5 attaches Dieudonné-Manin slopes to σ-modules over Γ_con (generic Newton polygon) and shows that the special polygon lies above the generic one with the same endpoint. Chapter 6 descends these filtrations to the Robba ring, producing a σ-module over Γ_con whose two polygons coincide.

Theorem 6.10, pp. 77-78, by induction on rank. Let s_1 be the lowest special slope with multiplicity m. Existence of M_1: take a Galois extension O'/O whose value group contains the special slopes. Proposition 6.9 gives K finite normal over k((t)) and a model M' over Γ^K_con[1/p] ⊗_O O' with equal generic and special polygons, and Proposition 5.16 gives its slope filtration with first step P_1. The top exterior power of P_1 is defined over Γ^alg_an,con and over Γ^K_an,con ⊗ O', hence over Γ^K_an,con. Galois descent over the maximal purely inseparable subextension K_1 (Corollary 3.16) and the slope bound of Proposition 4.5 give M_1 of rank m and single slope s_1; Frobenius iteration descends M_1 from K_1 to k((t)).

Theorem 6.10, continued: N_1 comes from the first step Q_1 of the Γ_con-filtration by Galois descent along Gal(K/K_1) × Gal(O'/O) and Frobenius iteration. Uniqueness of M_1 follows from Proposition 4.4 (eigenvectors of slope s_1 cannot survive in the quotient), and uniqueness of N_1 from Proposition 5.11.

Deduction of Theorem 1.1 (Section 6.4): after enlarging O and twisting so that s_i = 0, Theorem 6.12(d)-(e) shows that M_i and N_i are ∇-stable. N_i is then a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over Γ_con, to which Proposition 6.11 (Tsuzuki) applies; the auxiliary coefficient extension is removed afterwards.
acceptance: Unit-root case (Proposition 6.11): a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over Γ_con acquires a kernel of ∇ of full rank over Γ^K_con for a finite extension K of k((t)) that can be chosen separable if k is perfect and nearly separable otherwise, provided F acts on some basis over Γ^K_con by a matrix A with v_p(A - I) > 1/(p-1).

Bessel isocrystal (Section 1.5): generic slopes 0 and 1 but special slopes 1/2 and 1/2, so the special Newton polygon lies strictly above the generic one with the same endpoint. Any implementation of "slope" must distinguish the generic polygon (over Γ_con) from the special polygon (over Γ_an,con).

The filtration is unique given (a)-(b) of Theorem 6.10, and the N_i are unique. The source states no functoriality, so any functoriality that RD.1's slope-filtration contract requires must be derived from this uniqueness. A rank-one σ-module is the case l = 1.

links.reason: R06.3 must prove that de Rham representations are potentially semistable, and its atlas record requires RD.2. The consumer argument read (Berger, library copy arXiv v3, proof of Théorème 5.19, p. 58) uses the logarithmic form, not Theorem 1.1 as stated. It first reduces to k algebraically closed and Hodge-Tate weights ≤ 0, then applies Théorème 5.20 to N_dR(V): a finitely presented differential module over R_K = B†_rig,K with Frobenius structure has a basis of solutions over R_L[log π] for a finite extension L/K. Berger attributes Théorème 5.20 to André [2] and cites Kedlaya [32] only as another proof "par des méthodes très différentes". The export RD.2 must supply is therefore Kedlaya's Theorem 6.13 (recorded in this node) transported to Berger's ring R_K, Frobenius ϕ and derivation ∂. That transport, and the bridge from representations to N_dR(V) (Berger Théorèmes 3.6, 5.10 and §5.4), belong to R06.3 and have not been checked (see gap).
